newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore forex market continues to grow in 96-MAS.
newsitem.headline: Singapore forex market continues to grow in 96-MAS.

text.p: Singapore's foreign exchange market continued to grow in 1996 with the yen and the mark still the most actively traded currencies against the United States dollar, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Singapore's central bank, said in its annual report on Tuesday.
Average daily volume in 1996 was US$128.6 billion, up from US$109.2 billion in 1995, with dollar/yen and dollar/mark accounting for 20 percent and 17 percent of total turnover respectively.
During the first quarter of 1997 foreign exchange activity surged to US$187.7 billion per day.
In his introduction to the report, MAS Chairman and Minister of Finance Richard Hu said trading levels now exceeded US$190 billion a day.

In the options market transactions averaged US$33.9 billion per month in 1996, 9.8 percent down on 1995, with most accounted for by dollar/mark, dollar/yen and mark/yen. Around 83.8 percent of currency option trades were executed with counterparties outside Singapore.

The value of interest rate swap transactions averaged US$52.1 billion per month in 1996, 14 percent up on 1995 levels. U.S. dollar denominated swaps continued the most active, but their share of total swaps declined to 48 percent of the total from 58 percent in 1995.
Yen swaps made up 42 percent of the total, with swap transactions in other currencies rising by a bumper 155 percent in 1996 to make up the remaining 10 percent of the total swaps volume.

Turnover in forward rate agreements (FRAs) averaged US$30.0 billion monthly in 1996, a drop of 36 percent from the previous year. U.S. dollar FRAs made up 41 percent of total volume, 5 percent down on 1995 with yen deals down 32 percent in 1996.
However, yen FRAs share of total volume rose to 50 percent from 47 percent in 1995. FRAs in other currencies accounted for nine percent of total volume, two percent up on 1995.
